message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this ECG normal.** From the image, I see:

- An irregular rhythm at approximately **130 beats/minute**, without consistent visible P waves—concerning for **atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response**.
- Some prominent chest-lead waveforms and ST–T changes that need clinician review and comparison with any previous ECG.

The irregular rhythm and absent P waves are characteristic of atrial fibrillation, though a clinician should confirm this tracing. [ECG diagnostic features](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/specific-cardiac-arrhythmias/atrial-fibrillation)

**If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or new weakness/speech difficulty, seek emergency care now.** If you feel well and this is a new finding, arrange medical assessment today.

Is this your ECG, when was it taken, and are you having any symptoms?
